literal: Smile and joy which destroys, than anger, enemy are there other?
translation: Is there any other enemy greater than anger, which destroys both one's outward smile and inward joy?
modern: முகத்தில் தோன்றும் நகையையும் மனதில் தோன்றும் மகிழ்ச்சியையும் அழிக்கும் கோபத்தை விட வேறு கொடிய பகை உண்டோ?
explanation: This couplet highlights the destructive nature of anger by comparing it to an enemy. Anger is the ultimate enemy because it destroys two of a person's most precious qualities: their outward smile (நகை) and their inward joy (உவகை). The rhetorical question 'are there other enemies?' emphasizes that no external adversary can cause as much self-harm as one's own anger.
